A discoverability finding, not a schema one","source":"art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27","statement":"RUN AS THE SKILL on dev_storyflow's 2026-09-23 entry (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27), triage of 2026-09-28.

① OBSERVED, verbatim: `Invalid edge: VERIFIES cannot connect Verification to Decision`. "The live walk tested a ruling ... the only way to tie that check to the ruling is to write the ruling's id into the check's prose. A choice with conditions attached ('the label must say X', 'the chapter picker must not place a session') is exactly the kind of thing a test can confirm. I routed it to the requirement + capability instead, which loses the link to the conditions." Expected: a structured way to say this check bears on this ruling. NOT affected: VERIFIES to a Requirement or Capability.

② PRECEDENT (search on the raw refusal): Verification→Decision was never reported or ruled. The VERIFIES target list has been found short three times — the Requirement hint, Constraint (dec:should-a-verification-be-able-to-verify-a-constraint, 2026-08-15), Interface (chg:a-contract-can-carry-evidence, 2026-08-22) — and Project is still unruled (fact:dynograph-foundations-export-will-not-import-because-five-checks-verify-its-project). A check beside its ruling was already judged a legitimate pair on 2026-09-05 (fact:defect-two-prescribed-layer-pairs-are-missing-so-a-check-beside-its-ruling-is-refused-as-a-duplicate). "A typed helper refuses worse than create_edge" is recorded from flo2 F11 (fact:a-typed-edge-helper-given-a-wrong-typed-node-reports-it-absent-and-blames-a-race-that-did-not-happen).

③ CANDIDATES: (a) SCHEMA — VERIFIES' enumerated target list omits Decision, a fourth time the list is short (the reporter's reading). (b) DISCOVERABILITY — another edge already carries check→ruling and nothing pointed at it. (c) MODELLING — a ruling's conditions are meant to be their own nodes (DesignRule / Constraint / Requirement GOVERNED_BY the ruling); VERIFIES already admits DesignRule and Constraint. (d) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG — the reporter's requirement route did not actually lose the ruling in any computation.

④ DISCRIMINATOR: under (b), describe_schema{from: Verification, to: Decision} names an edge declared for the pair, a typed tool draws it, AND some computation reads a check→ruling edge; under (a) alone, nothing reads any such path. For (d): does the doubt walk reach a Decision through a requirement it governs?

⑤ RESULT, reflow2-mcp 0.72.0, scratch store: describe_schema → exact_matches 0, modelled_open_matches 1 = GOVERNED_BY (declared_for_this_pair: true, listed first). `governed_by {from_id: ver:…, to_id: dec:…}` drew it. With the decision accepted and the check set failing, `choices_in_doubt` returned that decision with evidence [ver:…] via [ver:…], kind recorded_failing. In code, doubt.rs walk_up starts AT the check, and held_up_under counts "governed checks themselves". ⇒ (b) HOLDS: the link is modelled, typed and READ. And the reason it went unseen, measured: the typed `verifies` refusal is exactly the bare sentence the reporter quoted, with no alternative; `create_edge` for the same pair lists GOVERNED_BY first as "the modelled fit"; `verifies`' description names 4 of its 7 targets (not DesignRule, Constraint or Interface); grep over every served SKILL.md finds no instruction linking a check to a ruling. (d) PARTLY: walk_up climbs VERIFIES → requirement → GOVERNED_BY, so the reporter's route still reaches the ruling IF their requirement is GOVERNED_BY it.

⑥ CLASS: the three-legs shape (fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it). The tool leg and the reader leg are present. The instruction leg is missing, and the typed helper's refusal, the one place it could have arrived, says less than the generic tool. It is also the 2026-09-08 triage's shape (fact:three-of-eight-reported-verification-gaps-were-already-built): a reported verification gap that already exists. Would the class fix have stopped the earlier report too? Yes. A typed helper returning create_edge's refusal would also have answered flo2 F11 (2026-09-19).

PINNING TEST (not written; code is out of scope for this triage): for every typed edge helper, a refused (from, to) pair returns the same accepting-edge list as create_edge for that pair, with the modelled_open_match first. Fails today on verifies(Verification→Decision).

GENUINELY OPEN, for the owner: GOVERNED_BY says the ruling SHAPES the check, not that the check CONFIRMS a named CONDITION. No detector asks whether an accepted ruling with conditions has any check, and coverage_report does not count one. Whether VERIFIES should admit Decision, as it admitted Constraint, is an unruled schema question like Project. It is not settled here.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: the reporter's graph (whether their requirement is GOVERNED_BY the ruling), and their binary on 09-23. The refusal text is identical on 0.72.0.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS: "the only way to tie that check to the ruling is prose" is OVERTURNED.
